info.title: Vision Service API
info.description:
Training runs, their epochs and results, and what is built on them: test results, benchmarks,
comparisons, visualizations and written findings. New here? Start with the
[quickstart](/docs/quickstart).

**Credentials.** Training scripts use a *pipeline key*: a personal API key limited to one project.
Other personal API keys can reach projects their owner may access, narrowed by their scopes.
Send either in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

**Responses.** Every path starts with `/api`. A request that works answers
`{ "success": true, "data": … }`; one that fails answers `{ "success": false, "error": …, "message": … }`
with the matching status.

**Privacy.** Projects default to private. A private project, its configurations and results are visible
to its owning person or owning group’s current members, and to members of its editor groups.
Public projects allow anonymous reads. Current group roles determine who can contribute, manage or transfer.

visinUrl.description: Your Visin API address. A local `docker compose up` answers at http://localhost:4010.

message.description: What went wrong, naming the field or record

configId.description: Configuration belonging to this training’s project.

revision.description: The version the run used. A Hub commit for a dataset kept on the Hub, otherwise the zip's upload time.

archiveRevision.description: For a dataset that is on the Hub and also has a zip on Visin, the zip's upload time. Recorded beside the commit, so a replaced zip is visible on runs that trained on it.

models.description: Hugging Face Hub models linked to this run. Visin keeps the pointer, never the bytes.

notes.description: The researcher's own commentary on the run ("this one used the relabelled night set"), apart from `description`, which says what the run is. Anyone who may write to the run may change it; an empty string removes it.

Provenance.description: What the run was started from, so it can be reproduced. Filled in by the pipeline's client; a credential in a remote URL is removed on receipt.

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes were present, so the commit alone does not name the code that ran.

command.description: The command line, with secrets redacted by the client.

Checkpoint.description:
Which bytes were scored. A Hub checkpoint is its repo, a full commit and optionally a file; a local one is
the SHA-256 of the weights that were loaded, never a path.

code.description: A stable code, listed with how to fix it in the Evaluations guide.

evidence.description:
How much the evaluator reported about the run. It labels a result and never decides whether it is ranked.
`observed`: it sent the data, the protocol digest and its own package and version, and each matched the
suite. `reported`: ranked on the submitter's word, with none or only some of that evidence (what was sent
matched). `attested`: a manager promoted an old result and vouched for it; nothing was observed, and none
is invented. `none`: no suite. Every level is the submitter's word, never verified.

state.description:
`eligible` may be ranked. `incomplete` lacks something the suite requires. `incompatible` measured
something other than the suite measures. `exploratory` named no suite. `legacy-unverified` predates suites.

scores.description: Present when eligible. Per condition and overall, for each metric the suite names.

EvaluationEvidence.description:
What was reported about the run. `observed` carries the evaluator's own evidence, which the suite is compared
against; `attested` records the manager who promoted an old result and the checkpoint and counts they
supplied. A promoted result never carries observed fields, because none were observed.

data.description: The data actually scored, in the shape a suite pins it.

protocolDigest.description: The digest of the protocol file the evaluator ran.

Evaluation.description:
What a reader may see depends on who they are. Someone in the project (who can add to it) sees everything. Anyone
else who can read it, because it is public, sees only results a manager published, without `ownerId`, without
who vouched for an attested result, and with only the evaluator of the run's `provenance`.

uuid.description: The writer's id, unique within the project.

ownerId.description: Who recorded it. Left out for a reader who is not in the project.

checkpointKey.description: `hf:<repo>@<commit>:<path>` or `sha256:<digest>`. Evaluations with one key are the same model.

source.description: Where the checkpoint came from. It says nothing about which bytes were scored.

evaluationId.description: The evaluation it was copied from, when it was promoted.

run.description: The run it came from, when that run is still live. Only in a list.

epochInfo.description: The epoch it was recorded at, when that epoch is still live. Only in a list.

suite.description: The suite version it was judged on, and that protocol's digest at the time.

executedAt.description: When the writer says it ran.

receivedAt.description: When the server stored it; this orders attempts.

publishedAt.description: Present when a manager put this result on its suite's public leaderboard.

verifiedAt.description: When a manager or an automated job verified this result. Verification does not control visibility.

verifiedBy.description: The verifying account; omitted for public readers.

hidden.description: Present when a manager of the suite took it off the suite's leaderboard.

supersedesId.description: The evaluation this one corrects. It must be of the same suite and checkpoint.

supersededById.description: The live correction that replaces this result. It is never ranked or published again.

results.description: Only on a single evaluation. The result as sent.

provenance.description: Only on a single evaluation. Submitter-reported; nothing here is verified.

DataTerms.description:
What the publisher says about the data a suite scores. A declaration shown beside the results, not part of the
protocol, so it is not hashed and a wrong one is corrected in place. Visin holds no copy of the data, and a
licence listed here is the publisher's word, not something Visin has checked. Absent on a suite means unstated,
which is not permission to use the data.

id.description: A listed licence id (the Hugging Face Hub spelling), or `other`.

url.description: The licence text. Always set for a listed licence.

commercial.description: false when the licence forbids commercial use. Absent for `other`.

sourceUrl.description: Where the data lives and its own terms are accepted.

credit.description: The credit line or citation the data asks for.

PublicSuite.description:
A suite as an anonymous reader sees it. A Visin dataset is reported only as `{ kind: visin }`: its id and digest
belong to the deployment and are not shown.

data.description: What the data is. `visin` carries nothing else; `hf` a repo and commit; `external` a label.

scope.description: The attempts behind the rows shown: every attempt of those checkpoints, published or not.

evidence.description: Evidence is reported by the submitter. Manager or job verification is recorded separately in verifiedAt.

conditions.description: The headline metric in each condition.

attempts.description: How many results this project recorded of this checkpoint on the suite, published or not.

evidenceLevel.description: Whether the evaluator sent complete evidence (observed), less (reported), or a manager vouched for an old result (attested).

evaluator.description: Only the evaluator's package, version and commit, when the submitter reported them.

evidenceLevel.description: Whether the evaluator sent complete evidence (observed), less (reported), or a manager vouched for an old result (attested).

selection.description: One evaluation per checkpoint, the latest eligible completed one by server arrival time. Never the best repeat.

scope.description: The pool that was ranked. A rank is a position within it, not among everything ever run.

truncated.description: The complete authorized pool is always ranked.

entries.description: Best first. Ties share a rank, and the next rank skips ("1, 2, 2, 4").

attempts.description: How many evaluations of this checkpoint were recorded, of any outcome.

evidenceLevel.description: How much the evaluator reported; see `validation.evidence`.

worst.description: The condition the headline is worst on, which for a `min` metric is its highest value.

gap.description: How far the worst condition falls short of the overall figure.

unranked.description: Checkpoints with attempts but none eligible, with the latest attempt's reasons.

SuiteProtocol.description:
What decides a score: the data, the conditions with their sample counts, the metrics and which way is
better, and how the overall figure is formed. It is hashed into the suite's `digest`, so changing any
field is a new version. The request form is `#/SuiteProtocol` in `generated/request-schemas.json`.

projectId.description: The project that published it, and whose access rules apply.

visibility.description: `public` lets anyone read the protocol; it grants nothing in the project.

submissions.description:
Who may publish results to its public leaderboard. `open`: a manager of any public project. `members`: only
the project that owns the suite. `approval`: any public project; managers review unverified submissions.
Verification is a label and does not control visibility.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical protocol. Two suites with one digest score identically.

archivedAt.description: Present once archived. New evaluations are refused; the suite and its results stay readable.

Submission.description: A published result as a manager of the suite sees another project's, with only what the public sees.

revision.description: The full commit hash the run produced. Never a branch or tag, so the link keeps naming the same bytes.

path.description: A file or folder inside the repo, when the model is not all of it.

epoch.description: The epoch the checkpoint came from.

space.description: A demo Space on the Hub where anyone can try the model, `org/name`. Set with `PATCH /trainings/{id}/models/{modelId}`.

results.description: What the epoch reported, as sent. Conditions, classes and metrics are discovered from it.

fileId.description: file-service storage path for the file.

lastActivityAt.description: When anything last happened in it; a project older than that field reads as its last edit

lastRunAt.description: When the latest run started; absent with no runs

PaperAuthor.description: One name on a paper's author list, as the paper prints it.

status.description:
Present when the name is linked to a Visin account. `confirmed`: that person accepted. `pending`: they have not
answered yet, which only the paper's managers and that person are told.

user.description: The linked account, as far as its owner agreed to be shown. Only an id when their profile is hidden.

PaperCard.description: A paper as a list shows it.

available.description: How many of them are public now.

ActivityItem.description: One line of a public activity feed. Always about a public project.

at.description: The latest start of that day

count.description: Runs started that UTC day in that project

readme.description: The project's front page, in Markdown. Left out of lists, and present when you open the project. Rendered as text and links only: no raw HTML, no images, no scripts.

createdBy.description: The account that created it. Attribution only; it grants nothing.

visibility.description: `public`: anyone can read it, signed in or not. `private`: its owner, the owning group's members, and editor groups.

editorGroupIds.description: Groups the project is shared with. Their current members get `contribute`. Changing the list takes `manage`.

trashedAt.description: Set while it is in the trash.

purgeAt.description: In the trash listing, when it will be deleted for good.

storage.description: Where the project keeps its big files. Absent means `visin`. Changing it takes `manage`.

provider.description: `visin`: everything stays on this deployment, and a run's links to Hub models and its references to Hub datasets (`dataset.source: hf`) are refused with `409`. `hf`: runs may link Hugging Face Hub models and train on Hub datasets. A Visin dataset that is itself kept on the Hub is governed by the dataset, not by this setting.

settings.description: What the provider keeps about the project, validated by that provider. Replaces the whole setting, so leaving it out clears it.

namespace.description: For `hf`, the Hub user or organisation a pipeline should create repos under by default.

ResourceOwner.description: A person, or a group whose members' current roles decide who may do what.

name.description: A group's name, when you are in it; a person's name, as they agreed to show it.

handle.description: A person's handle, the address of their public page (/u/{handle}). Absent when they hid their profile.

picture.description: A person's avatar, when they have one and agreed to show it.

ProjectPermissions.description:
What you may do with the project. Each level includes the ones before it.
`read`: see it. `contribute`: add runs, results and findings, and change your own
(a group member, or an editor group). `manage`: settings, anyone's runs, the
trash (a group admin). `own`: who can see it, transfer, restore or delete it for
good (its owner, or the owning group's owner).

BearerCredential.description:
A user API key (`vsn_live_…`) or an assistant's OAuth access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
A key can be limited to one project, which is what a training pipeline uses: it then reaches only that
project, runs it creates land there whatever project the request names, and it cannot manage projects.

SessionCookie.name: access_token
SessionCookie.description: The signed-in browser session. Not for scripts.

BadRequest.description: The request was rejected by validation

NotFound.description: The requested resource does not exist

Unauthorized.description: No credential, or one that is invalid, expired or revoked

Forbidden.description: The credential is valid but may not do this

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, for example a project whose storage does not allow it

Error.description: The request failed; the status and message say why

get.description:
Includes public projects and the authenticated user's own projects.
Visibility and subject/citation filters apply before the limit. Results
are ordered by createdAt descending, then _id descending to break ties.
To continue, set before to the last row's createdAt + "_" + _id, keeping
the same filters. Example: 2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z_507f1f77bcf86cd799439011.
Stop when a page has fewer than limit rows; a full final page may be
followed by an empty page. The response data remains an array.
The cursor still works if its row is deleted. Each page reapplies current
visibility; this is not a snapshot. Refresh to see newly added findings
above the cursor or findings made visible since an earlier page.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project slug or ID; an inaccessible project returns 403.

parameters.name: training
parameters.description: Matches the finding's subject training or a cited training.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The previous page's final createdAt (UTC ISO timestamp with milliseconds), underscore, and lowercase 24-character ObjectId.

200.description: One page of visible findings, including visible cited training names.

403.description: The selected project is not visible to this caller.

404.description: The selected project does not exist.

post.description: A written conclusion about one or more runs in a project. The caller must be able to edit the project.

403.description: The caller cannot edit this project.

200.description: The finding, with the cited trainings the caller can see

403.description: The finding's project is not visible to this caller.
The caller cannot edit this finding's project.

get.description:
The finding as a `.tex` section with a results table of its cited runs.
Returned as JSON rather than a file download, so the app and an assistant
can both use it. `selectBy` names the metric that decides which epoch each
run is reported at, and `direction` says which end of it is better.

200.description: The LaTeX source and a suggested file name

403.description: The finding's project is not visible to this caller.

parameters.name: access
parameters.description: `contribute` keeps only runs in projects you can write to, leaving out other people's public work.

post.description:
Start a run before posting its epochs. Send your own `uuid` to refer to the
run by an id your script already knows; one is generated otherwise.

Every run belongs to a project: `projectId` (its id or slug) is required, except
with a credential limited to a project, where the run goes into that project and
`projectId` is ignored. A project that does not exist, or that you cannot see,
answers 404 with its name; create it under Projects first. Adding a run takes
`contribute` on the project.

A `dataset` with `source: hf` answers 409 unless the project's storage is set to Hugging Face.

get.summary: The best run of a project or a dataset
get.description:
Names the run that did best, and says by what: a run is only the best at something, so the answer carries the
`metric` it was judged on and the direction. Pass a `projectId` for one project, or a `datasetId` for every run
trained on that dataset in the projects the caller can see.

The result a project is judged on is its taxonomy's `primaryMetric` (`metric.source: project`). Without one
it is guessed: a quality score such as `val.mean_iou` from the validation block, else the validation loss
(`metric.source: guessed`). A project whose runs report nothing that reads as a score has no best run, and
`best` is `null`. Direction follows the taxonomy as in the training summary. Across projects whose results
differ, the result used by most of the dataset's runs decides, since a loss and an IoU cannot be compared.

Runs still training count, at the best epoch they have reached so far.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: A project’s id or slug

parameters.name: datasetId
parameters.description: A Visin dataset id the runs were trained on

200.description: The best run, or `null` when none can be named

get.description:
Cost estimates use each project's current CPU/GPU rates. Amounts are
grouped by currency without exchange-rate conversion. Legacy scalar cost
fields and currency are present only when exactly one currency is priced.
Coverage includes unpriced trainings and measured durations in seconds;
zero rates count as priced. These are current estimates, not historical bills.

currency.description: ISO currency code of the optional scalar costs

costTotalsByCurrency.description: One subtotal per currency, sorted by currency code; empty if unpriced

get.description: Every tag on a training the caller can see, for filter suggestions.

put.description: A `dataset` with `source: hf` answers 409 unless the project's storage is set to Hugging Face.

get.summary: List deleted trainings the caller can restore
get.description: Most recently deleted first: the caller’s runs in projects they contribute to, and all runs in projects they manage. Requires a signed-in caller.

post.description: Brings the training back with the epochs and test results its delete removed. Rows deleted separately beforehand stay deleted, and the training is not re-added to comparisons it was removed from.

get.description:
Resolves a non-deleted training and checks its project visibility before
returning its selected config, whose project must also be readable.
Public projects allow anonymous reads; private projects require access through
its owner, the owning group, or an editor group. Project-limited keys are
additionally restricted to their own project.

403.description: The caller cannot access this training's project

post.description: Unordered insertion saves every new epoch even if another UUID already exists. The data array contains inserted epochs; existing contains repeated UUIDs. Other database or validation errors still fail the request.

Post one epoch of a run, usually at the end of each epoch in the training loop.
Name the run with `training_uuid` (or its `trainingId`); it must already exist,
so create it with `POST /trainings` first.

`results` is stored as sent. The run's charts read `train` and `val` (the training and validation
curves) and the metrics under them, such as `loss` and `mean_iou`; a key under `val` or `train` that
holds metrics such as `iou` is a class, found without being declared. A metric an epoch did not
report is left out, not sent as `0`. See /docs/sending-results for every name the charts read.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the epoch together with the test results recorded against it.

data.description: With `page` or `limit`, a page and its `pagination`; without, every epoch and their `total`.

post.description:
A configuration belongs to a project and is seen by whoever can read that project.
`projectId` (its id or slug) is required, except with a credential limited to a
project, which supplies its own.

get.description: The same listing as for one training, over every training the caller can see.
For each visible training, how many visualizations it has of each type and at which epochs. No images or signed URLs.

200.description: One entry per training that has visualizations, newest first

post.description:
A comparison with a `projectId` follows that project. One without is personal:
only its creator sees it, only while they can read every project its items come
from, and a credential limited to a project cannot make one.

parameters.name: access
parameters.description: `contribute` keeps only projects you can write to (yours, and those your groups edit), leaving out other people's public projects.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: `me`, or a group id: only the projects that owner has.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: A person's id: only the projects that person owns, of those you may read. What a public profile lists.

post.description:
It belongs to you, or with `owner` to a group you are in. Only a group's owner can
make one of its projects public.

get.summary: Get project by ID or slug

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Project id or slug

delete.summary: Move a project to the trash
delete.description:
Hidden at once, with its runs. Its owner can restore it for 30 days; after that it
is deleted for good with everything in it. Takes `manage`.

put.description:
Hand the project, with everything in it, to another owner. You can move your own
project to a group you are in (one way); a group's owner can move the group's
project to one of its members, or to another group they are in.

post.summary: Report that a training is alive
post.description: Refreshes server receipt time. A stalled run resumes; completed and failed runs remain terminal.

post.summary: Link a Hugging Face model to a training
post.description:
Records a pointer to a model on the Hub, pinned to the commit a run produced. Visin stores the reference,
not the checkpoint: upload it where it was trained, with your own Hugging Face token, then report it here.

Repeating the same repo, commit and path is a no-op that returns `200`, so a pipeline can retry freely.
The project's storage must be set to `hf` (project settings); a `visin` project answers `409`. A run links
at most 50 models. Needs write access to the run.

patch.summary: Link a demo Space to a model
patch.description: Records, or clears with `null`, the Hugging Face Space where anyone can try this model. Visin does not check that the Space exists. Needs write access to the run.

parameters.name: modelId
parameters.description: The `_id` of the link, from the training's `models`.

delete.summary: Unlink a model from a training
delete.description: Removes the pointer only; nothing on the Hub is touched. Allowed whatever the project's storage is now.

parameters.name: modelId
parameters.description: The `_id` of the link, from the training's `models`.

get.description:
Every Hugging Face Hub model linked to a run the caller may see, one row per link. This is what to open to
answer "which model should I use": filter by project or dataset, and rank by how well each run did on a
result of your choice.

With `metric`, a row carries two scores that are not the same thing. `best` is where the *run* peaked on the
result. `checkpoint` is what the epoch the link names (`model.epoch`) reported, so a checkpoint saved at epoch
12 is not credited with the epoch-40 peak. A link that names its epoch is ranked by `checkpoint` alone, and is
listed last when that epoch did not report the result. A link without an epoch is ranked by `best`.

Visin does not know whether a result is better high or low, so `direction` is yours to give. A project-limited
key sees only its own project.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: A project id or slug.

parameters.name: datasetId
parameters.description: A Visin dataset id the run was trained on.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches a run name or a model repo, ignoring case.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Rank by this result, e.g. `val.mean_iou`. Adds `best` (the run's peak) and, for a link that names its epoch, `checkpoint` (that epoch's value) to each row.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Whether larger is better for `metric`. Use `min` for a loss or a latency.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: `addedAt` (default) or `best`, which needs `metric`. Ranks by `checkpoint` for a link that names its epoch, else by `best`. A link with no score is listed last.

best.description: Present when `metric` was given and the run reported it.

checkpoint.description:
Present when `metric` was given, the link names its epoch (`model.epoch`) and that epoch
reported the result. The value is that epoch's, not the run's peak.

evaluations.description:
What this checkpoint scored on suites: its latest eligible evaluation on each suite
version, as the suite's headline figure. The checkpoint is matched by its canonical key
(`hf:<repo>@<revision>:<path>`), never by model name or epoch, so a Hub link and a
local weights digest are different checkpoints. Only evaluations in projects the
caller may read count, and a credential limited to one project sees only that
project's. Absent when there are none.

get.summary: Rank readable recorded results, including migrated evaluations
get.description:
Includes completed recorded scores without a suite. Uses normal evaluation access permissions, so private
projects remain private. Selects the latest completed live result per project, suite and checkpoint or run,
then filters verification and ranks the selected metric. Different data remains labelled by project and run.
Verification is a label, not a condition for inclusion. Scores with no value for the selected metric are omitted.

200.description: Recorded scores ranked and paginated after verification filtering

post.summary: Set or remove verification on a result
post.description:
A manager of the result's project, or an automated job using their project-scoped API key, sets verification.
True stamps `verifiedAt` and `verifiedBy` on the server; false clears both. Repeating the same action is harmless.
Verification does not change the score, protocol validation or publication. Public readers see the timestamp,
but never the account id. Needs `manage` on the project.

get.description:
Evaluations in the projects the caller may read, newest first. In a project the caller is part of, all of them; in a
public project they are not part of, only the published ones, without who recorded them. Result blobs and
provenance are left out; open one to read them, or ask for `include=results` on a small page.

What a run reported is here too: a result recorded without a suite (a test), and one scored on a suite, both
carry the run (`run`) and epoch (`epochInfo`) they came from when those are still live. Filter by run with
`trainingId` or `trainingUuid`, and by epoch with `epoch` or `epochUuids`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: A project id or slug.

parameters.name: suite
parameters.description: Only evaluations on this suite version, as `slug@version`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only evaluations in this validation state.

parameters.name: trainingId
parameters.description: Only what came from this run, by its id.

parameters.name: trainingUuid
parameters.description: Only what came from the run with this uuid. A run that is gone or not visible has nothing to list.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: Only what was recorded at this epoch number.

parameters.name: epochUuids
parameters.description: Only what came from any of these epochs, as comma separated epoch uuids.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Newest first by default; `executedAt` is when the writer says it ran, `epoch` the epoch it came from.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `results` carries each evaluation's results, which a list leaves out. Use it with a small page.

post.description:
Record one checkpoint's results, optionally against a suite version. Name the project, or leave it out and name
the epoch the result came from (`source.epochUuid`): a run's pipeline knows its epoch, and the epoch's project is
the run's. A result recorded without a suite (a test a run reports) is stored and shown but not ranked. The
server judges the result and stores
the verdict in `validation`: a well-formed result that cannot be ranked is kept, with the reasons, rather than
refused. A malformed body, a credential in `provenance`, an unknown suite or an archived one is refused.

Send your own `uuid`. The same result again answers `200` with the stored evaluation, so a retry after a lost
response is safe; a different result under that uuid is `409`. To correct a result, send a new one with
`supersedesId`, of the same suite and the same checkpoint: the corrected result is then replaced by the
correction and leaves the ranking even when the correction cannot be ranked. One live correction at a time can
replace a result (`409` otherwise); trashing the correction gives the original its place back. Results never
change.

A Hub checkpoint needs a project whose storage is Hugging Face. Needs `contribute` on the project.

200.description: This result was already recorded under this uuid

post.summary: Rank a result you already have
post.description:
Copy a result recorded without a suite (a test a run reported) onto one, so it can be ranked without being run
again. The evaluation it is copied from is not changed: its results are copied as they are, and the new evaluation
records the run, epoch and evaluation it came from, with provenance saying it was promoted.

A result recorded without a suite carries no checkpoint identity and no sample counts, so you supply both. What you
supply is yours to vouch for. The verdict is computed like any other, and a result that cannot be ranked is stored
with its reasons.

Promoting the same evaluation onto the same suite again returns the first (`200`). A different checkpoint, or
different sample counts, for it is `409` until that evaluation is trashed; a failed evaluation, or one already
judged on that suite, is `409` too. Needs `manage` on the evaluation's project.

200.description: This evaluation was already promoted onto this suite

post.summary: Publish an evaluation to its public leaderboard
post.description:
Put one ranked result on the public leaderboard of its suite. Publishing is a decision about a single result: a
public project or suite does not publish anything by existing.

Only a ranked, completed result can be published, in a **public project** and on a **public suite**; otherwise
`409` says which. Only the checkpoint's **latest** ranked result on the suite can be published, because a
leaderboard shows each checkpoint by its latest result: publishing an earlier, better one would let the best of
several attempts stand in for the model, so it is `409`. A result replaced by a correction cannot be published
either. Recording a newer ranked result of a checkpoint withdraws its earlier published ones, and the newer one
is published on its own. Needs `manage` on the project. The public views re-check all of it on every read, so
withdrawing, trashing, or making the project or suite private removes the result at once. Publishing again is
harmless. The change is recorded in the project's history.

What becomes public is limited to a fixed set of fields. See `GET /public/evaluations/{id}`.

post.summary: Take an evaluation off the public leaderboard
post.description: Removes it from every public list and detail at once. Withdrawing one that is not published changes nothing. Needs `manage` on the project.

post.summary: Approve a result submitted to a suite
post.description:
Compatibility action for a suite manager to verify a published result. Sets the same `verifiedAt` and
`verifiedBy` fields as the verification action; it does not control visibility. Needs `manage` on the suite's
project. An unpublished result is `409`; an already verified result answers `200`.

post.summary: Hide a published result from a suite's leaderboard
post.description:
A manager of the suite's own project can take any published result off the suite's public leaderboard, whichever
project it is from. The reason is kept with it, and the change is recorded. Its submitter can still see it and
withdraw it, but cannot publish it again until a manager shows it. Needs `manage` on the suite's project.

post.summary: Show a hidden result on its suite's leaderboard again
post.description: Needs `manage` on the suite's project. Its publisher's decision to publish it is still in force, so it stands on the board again. Unhiding one that is not hidden changes nothing.

get.description:
Papers anyone can open, a page at a time. The same for everyone who asks, so a signed-in author's drafts never mix
in. A person's list holds only the papers they have confirmed they wrote. Anonymous, never cached, and rate limited
by client address.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words in the title, abstract, authors, tags or venue; or an arXiv id or a DOI, in any spelling.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: A person's id. Only papers that person has confirmed they wrote.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project's id. Only papers citing a result in it.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `created` (default): newest added first. `year`: newest publication year first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Papers per page (default 12, at most 50).

get.description:
The projects anyone can open, a page at a time, as cards: owner (as far as the owner agreed to be shown), the number
of runs and when the latest started. The same for everyone who asks, so a signed-in member's own private projects
never mix in. Anonymous, never cached, and rate limited by client address.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words in the name or description.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `updated` (default): the most recent activity first (a run or epoch, a finding, a result, a change of settings). `created`: newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Projects per page (default 12, at most 50).

get.summary: The latest findings in public projects
get.description:
Written conclusions, newest first, from public projects only, the same for everyone who asks: a member's findings in
their own private projects are not here. Never the body, and never which account wrote one. Anonymous, never cached.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Findings to return (default 5, at most 20).

get.summary: What a person or a group has been doing in public
get.description:
Newest first: projects made, findings posted, runs started (one line per project per UTC day, not one per run) and
results recorded. Derived on each request from what is stored rather than from a log, so it is never stale, and a
project made private or trashed takes its whole history out of it at once. Only public projects count, whoever asks,
and of the evaluations only what a reader of a public project is shown (its runs' tests, and what a manager
published). Anonymous, never cached, and rate limited by client address.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: A person's account id. Give this or `owner`, not both.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: A group's id: everything in the public projects that group owns. Give this or `user`, not both.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Lines to return (default 30, at most 100).

get.description:
The suites that have at least one published, ranked result, newest activity first. Anonymous, and the same for
everyone: a credential in the request is not read. Never cached (`Cache-Control: no-store`), so a withdrawal is
not left standing anywhere, and rate limited by client address.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page of selected ranked summaries (default 1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Summaries per page (default and maximum 100).

get.description:
The ranking of one suite version over its published results. One row per checkpoint and project, from the
checkpoint's latest ranked attempt, never its best, and only when that very attempt is published: a newer ranked
attempt that is not published takes the row off the board until it is. Another project's result for the same
checkpoint is its own row. Ties share a rank; direction comes from the suite. `attempts` counts every attempt
the project recorded, published or not. `evidence` says the results are the submitters' own claims.

A suite that is private, absent or in a trashed project is `404`. Anonymous, never cached, rate limited.
Selection, attempt counts and ranks use the complete authorized pool before paging the summaries.
Ranks are global within that pool, including ties across page boundaries.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A version number. `latest` is not accepted, so a link keeps meaning one protocol.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page of selected ranked summaries (default 1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Summaries per page (default and maximum 100).

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description:
`observed` ranks only the results whose evaluator reported what it observed. The pool, its counts and the
ranks are then those of the observed results alone; promoted results are left out.

get.summary: Get the evidence behind a public entry
get.description:
The scores, sample counts, checkpoint and evaluator of one published result, and nothing else: no commands,
hosts, environment, raw configuration, run or user ids, or private dataset names. One that is not published, or
whose project or suite is no longer public, is `404`. Published evidence remains addressable even when
it is superseded in the ranking or falls outside the current leaderboard page.

get.summary: A badge for a published checkpoint
get.description:
A small SVG, such as `road-test v1 | mIoU 0.7351 · rank 2/9`, for one checkpoint published to one public
suite version, to embed in a README or a model card. It says nothing the public leaderboard page does not,
and it is `404` for anything that is not currently published there (a withdrawn, trashed or never published
result, a private suite or project), whatever the reason. Anonymous, never cached, rate limited.

Two projects can each publish the same checkpoint, so the badge names the project whose row it shows
(`project`, its slug or id); a badge for another project's row is a different badge.

`checkpointKey` is the canonical key, URL-encoded because it holds `:`, `@` and `/`:
`hf:<repo>@<commit>:<path>` for a Hub checkpoint (the repo in lower case, the path empty when there is none) or
`sha256:<digest>` for weights held elsewhere.

parameters.name: checkpointKey
parameters.description: The checkpoint's canonical key, URL-encoded.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The project whose published row the badge shows, by slug or id.

post.summary: Check a result without recording it
post.description:
Judge a result exactly as recording it would, and store nothing. Use it before an expensive upload to learn why
a result would be unranked. It needs the same access as recording, and the same readable suite.

get.summary: Get an evaluation by your own uuid
get.description: For recovering after a lost response. A uuid is unique within a project, so the project is part of the address.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: A project id or slug.

200.description: The evaluation, with its results and provenance

get.description: One that does not exist, is in the trash, or is in a project the caller may not read answers `404`.

200.description: The evaluation, with its results and provenance

delete.summary: Move an evaluation to the trash
delete.description:
A trashed evaluation leaves every list and leaderboard. Needs `manage`, or `contribute` for one the caller
recorded. Bring it back with `POST /evaluations/{id}/restore`.

get.description:
The suites the caller may read: those of projects they can read, and public suites of live projects. Newest
version first within a name. Archived suites are left out unless `includeArchived` is `true`.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Only the versions of this suite.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: A project id or slug.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Version order within a name.

post.description:
Publish a scoring protocol. A published version never changes, so a score on `slug@version` always means
the same thing.

Publishing the same protocol again returns the stored suite with `200`, so a pipeline's setup script can
run every time. A different protocol under a version that exists is `409`: publish it as the next version.
A `slug` is one name per deployment. Ownership is reserved atomically before inserting a version, so
concurrent publishes by different projects return `409` for the losing project even at different versions.
The reservation survives insertion failures and project purges; only the original project may retry a failed
insertion. Names cannot be reassigned. Existing suites acquire reservations lazily; conflicting historical
ownership returns `409` and requires operator resolution without rewriting published protocols.

`dataTerms` says what the evaluated data is licensed under, where it lives and how to credit it. Say it
for data you did not make: Visin shows it on the leaderboard beside the scores and holds no copy of the data.
A new version does not inherit it from the last, because the data may have changed; a retried publish of an
existing version leaves the stored one alone (correct it with `PATCH`).

Creating a private version needs `contribute` on the project. Creating a public version needs `manage`,
whether `visibility: public` is explicit or inherited. The first version defaults to private; a new version
inherits the highest existing version's visibility unless specified. A contributor can explicitly choose
`visibility: private`; inherited public visibility otherwise returns `403`.

Existing-version retries return the stored metadata, including visibility, without changing it or recording
another disclosure event. Initial public creation is recorded as a visibility event.
A key limited to one project can publish to that project only. With write scope, it may create a public suite
there when its actor has `manage`; the key itself grants no extra sharing permission.

200.description: This protocol was already published under this version

post.summary: Compute the digest of a protocol without publishing it
post.description:
The digest the server would store for this protocol, and the protocol with its defaults filled in. Nothing is
stored. An evaluator calls this with the protocol file it is about to run and sends the digest back as
`evidence.protocolDigest`, so the digest comes from the file actually used. The server alone canonicalizes
(defaults filled in, keys sorted), so clients never reimplement it.

protocol.description: The protocol with defaults filled in.

get.summary: Unverified and hidden results on a suite
get.description:
For a manager of the suite's own project: published results without verification, and the ones hidden from
its leaderboard, each with the checkpoint, the
submitting project's name and the headline score, and nothing else of that project's records. Needs `manage` on the
suite's project; a suite the caller cannot read is `404`.
A suite that does not exist and one the caller may not read both answer `404`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A version number, or `latest` for the highest one that is not archived.

patch.summary: Rename, reword, share or archive a suite
patch.description:
The protocol cannot change. `dataTerms` (the licence, source and credit of the evaluated data) can, because it
describes the data rather than how it is scored; `null` takes it back. Archiving stops new evaluations and keeps every result readable. Needs `manage`
on the project, or `contribute` on a suite the caller published; changing `visibility` or `submissions` needs
`manage`. Making a suite private ends the publication of every result on it, so making it public again does not
publish them afresh; changing `submissions` leaves what is published as it is.

get.summary: Rank the evaluations of a suite version
get.description:
One row per checkpoint: its latest eligible completed evaluation by server arrival time, never its best
repeat. Direction comes from the suite. Ties share a rank. Checkpoints with attempts but none eligible are
listed under `unranked` with their reasons.

The pool is the evaluations of this suite version in projects the caller may read, and `scope` says how many
there were, so a rank is a position within that pool and not among everything ever run.
Selection, attempt counts and ranks use the complete authorized pool before paging the summaries.
Ranks are global within that pool, including ties across page boundaries.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A version number, or `latest` for the highest one that is not archived.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page of selected ranked summaries (default 1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Summaries per page (default and maximum 100).

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description:
`observed` ranks only the results whose evaluator reported what it observed. The pool, its counts and the
ranks are then those of the observed results alone; promoted results are left out.

parameters.name: unrankedPage
parameters.description: Independent page of unranked checkpoints (default 1).

get.description:
The README a Hugging Face model repo should carry, written from what Visin recorded for the run: its dataset
and commit, the epoch reached, headline results, per-condition test results and speed. The front matter is the
Hub's `model-index`, so the scores show on the model page; it is left out when the project's task type does
not name a Hub task. No config values are included, since a config can hold anything.

`visin.Run.log_model` fetches this and uploads it as `README.md` when the repo has none.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: The Hub repo the card will sit in; names the card.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: The epoch the checkpoint came from. The latest reported epoch when absent.

200.description: The card, as Markdown with YAML front matter

get.summary: How a run did, in one call
get.description:
The run's state, dataset, config, linked models and provenance, and for every result it reported (the
shallowest numeric entries of an epoch's blocks, such as `val.mean_iou`, plus any top-level result, leaving out
per-class rows, telemetry nested below the summaries and bookkeeping like `lr`) the best epoch beside the last. A run's last
epoch is not its result, so both are given.

"Best" follows the project's taxonomy: a metric the project marked `higher` or `lower` is read that way
(`directionFrom: taxonomy`). Any other is guessed from its name, so a loss or a latency is lower-is-better
and the rest higher (`directionFrom: default`); check `directionFrom` before trusting a guess. At most 60
results are listed.

get.summary: Where the rest of this deployment is, and what your credential is
get.description:
What a client needs to set itself up from this one address: the dataset service's and the web app's public
addresses (each left out when the deployment has not configured it), and, for the credential sent, what
kind it is and what it can do. `visin login` uses it, so a researcher enters one address and one key.

Open to anyone. With no credential the kind is `anonymous`; a browser session is `session`; a user API key is
`api-key`; an API key limited to one project is `pipeline-key`, with that project. An API key's `scopes` say
what it may do.

200.description: The deployment and the caller's credential

get.summary: Export a comparison of trainings as a spreadsheet
get.description:
One row per run: its name, status, dataset, epochs and linked models, then for every result any of them
reported (the shallowest numeric entries of an epoch's blocks, such as `val.mean_iou`, plus any top-level result, leaving out
per-class rows, telemetry nested below the summaries and bookkeeping like `lr`) its best value, the epoch
that was reached at, the last value, and which way better was read. "(assumed)" after the direction marks
one guessed from the result's name rather than set in the project's taxonomy.

`csv` is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel reads accents correctly; text that a spreadsheet would
run as a formula is made inert. `xlsx` keeps numbers as numbers. A run the caller may not read, or that has
been deleted, is left out. Only a comparison of trainings can be exported: any other kind answers `400`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `xlsx` (the default) or `csv`.
